q: During claims inspection, the inspector first verifies that every claim received has been ___ in the claims register.
A break in the serial numbering of the claims register suggests that a case may have been ___.
The primary objective of claims inspection is to verify that claims are settled ___.

options.C: correctly, promptly and under proper authority

q: Compensation on a claim is admissible only when the loss occurred while the goods were ___.
A claim not preferred within the prescribed limitation period is treated as ___.
Notice of a claim for compensation for loss of goods must ordinarily be served within six months of ___.

options.B: entrustment of the goods to the railway

q: Open delivery is taken at destination when the packages appear ___.
A shortage certificate is issued at the destination station to record ___.
During inspection, paid claim vouchers are test-checked to confirm payment was made to the ___.
Re-weighment at destination is ordered when the consignee disputes the ___.
The inspector verifies that compensation is assessed on the basis of ___.
Outstanding claims statements are scrutinised to detect ___.
A claim for damage noticed at the time of delivery must be supported by ___.
The inspector checks that claims paid registers are reconciled with ___.
Fictitious claims are often detected by verifying the genuineness of ___.

options.C: the railway receipts and supporting documents

q: When a consignment is delivered short, the inspector checks that the claim is preferred by the ___.

options.D: consignee or the endorsed holder of the railway receipt

q: Assessment delivery differs from open delivery in that it is taken ___.

options.A: to assess the extent of damage for claim purposes

q: The claims inspector's diary should record ___.

options.B: points noticed during inspection for follow-up

q: Delay in settling a genuine claim may expose the railway to ___.
An appeal against rejection of a claim is examined to see whether the rejection was ___.

options.D: speaking, reasoned and as per rules

q: The inspector verifies that every claim case file contains ___.
Compensation for total non-delivery of a consignment is generally limited to ___.

options.B: the value of the goods lost, subject to legal limits

q: A claim preferred by an agent is valid only if supported by ___.

options.C: proper authority or power of attorney

q: During inspection, the inspector test-checks a sample of ___ cases rather than every case.
The register of claims paid should show ___ against each entry.

options.A: voucher number and date of payment

q: Where goods are carried at owner's risk, the railway's liability for compensation is ___.

options.B: restricted as per the risk note and law

q: The inspector ensures that claims arising from accidents are dealt with ___.
Overcharge claims differ from compensation claims because they relate to ___.
A second claim on the same railway receipt should be detected by checking ___.

options.A: the claims register for the RR number

q: The inspector verifies that refunds of freight on claims are credited to ___.
When perishable goods deteriorate in transit, compensation depends on ___.

options.C: whether the railway failed in its duty of care

q: Statistical returns of claims help management to identify ___.

options.D: trends in losses and weak areas

q: The inspector checks that time-barred claims rejected are ___.
Settlement of a claim without proper investigation is objectionable because it may lead to ___.

options.B: payment of inadmissible or inflated claims

q: The delivery book at the destination is checked against shortage certificates to ensure ___.
A claim for delay in delivery of goods is admissible subject to ___.

options.D: proof of actual loss caused by the delay

q: Inspectors pay special attention to claims settled for round sums because they may indicate ___.
The competent authority for sanctioning compensation depends on ___.

options.B: the amount involved, per the delegation of powers

q: Unloading and transhipment records are examined to trace ___.

options.C: the point where loss or damage occurred

q: Follow-up of inspection reports on claims is necessary to ensure ___.

options.D: objections are rectified and recoveries effected

q: A claim for pilferage en route is scrutinised with reference to ___.
The inspector verifies that claims received by post are ___.

options.B: entered in the register on receipt

q: Compensation paid through bank should be verified with ___.

options.C: the bank scroll or payment advice

q: Where the consignee takes delivery under protest, the inspector expects to find ___.

options.D: the protest recorded on the delivery documents

q: The inspector checks that claims staff do not ___.

options.A: settle claims in which they have a personal interest

q: A suit for compensation against the railway is generally subject to the law of ___.
The inspector test-checks that legal notices received are ___.

options.C: replied to in time and properly recorded

q: Recoveries from staff held responsible for losses are watched to ensure they are ___.
Claims for loss of luggage must be supported by ___.

options.A: the luggage ticket or other proof of booking

q: The inspector ensures that decrees of courts in claim suits are ___.

options.B: satisfied in time and charged to the proper head

q: A claim settled after the claimant's death requires payment to the ___.

options.C: legal heir on production of proof

q: The inspector verifies that part-settlement of a claim is ___.

options.D: clearly recorded with the balance position stated

q: Excessive outstanding claims at a station may point to ___.
The inspector checks that claims inspection reports of previous inspections have been ___.

options.B: complied with and old objections cleared

q: Where goods are delivered to the wrong person, the railway may face ___.

options.C: a claim for non-delivery from the rightful consignee

q: The claims register should be reviewed periodically by ___.
A consolidated statement of claims helps the inspector to ___.

options.A: judge the overall position at a glance

q: The inspector verifies that compensation for damage is reduced by ___.

options.B: the salvage value of the damaged goods

q: Claims preferred on forged railway receipts are detected by ___.

options.C: verification with the forwarding station's records

q: The ultimate aim of claims inspection is to ___.

options.D: protect railway revenue through correct and prompt settlement
